evidence.excerpt: We plan on doubling our AI talent to 80,000 people and expect to invest in assets, industry solutions, ventures and acquisitions.
evidence.review_reason: Future doubling of the AI talent pool; the target is not an attained workforce stock.

evidence.excerpt: We appointed a Chief AI Officer, launched a global generative AI Center of Excellence, and created comprehensive AI training for our entire workforce.
evidence.review_reason: Appointments, a center of excellence and workforce training are people/innovation actions.

evidence.excerpt: We have already trained approximately 600,000 of our people in the fundamentals of AI.
evidence.review_reason: Completed foundational training is reported, with an approximate participant count.

evidence.excerpt: We invested in our people to continue to develop their market-relevant skills and to help us reinvent our services using generative AI.
evidence.review_reason: Investment in people and skills, without a specific completed operational workflow.

classifier.label: deployment
classifier.rule: present use or completed release cue

evidence.excerpt: Our people had approximately 44 million training hours this year, representing an increase of 10% compared with fiscal 2023, predominantly due to generative AI training.
evidence.review_reason: Reported training hours and year-on-year change describe capability investment.

evidence.excerpt: We also continue to steadily increase our Data & AI workforce, reaching approximately 57,000 skilled Data & AI practitioners at the end of fiscal 2024, against our goal of doubling our Data & AI workforce to 80,000 by the end of fiscal 2026.
evidence.review_reason: Reported Data & AI practitioner stock is distinct from the future 80,000-person target.

evidence.excerpt: We are also empowering creators by putting the power of artificial intelligence (“AI”) in their hands, and doing so in ways we believe are responsible.
evidence.review_reason: Broad statement about empowering creators, with no named operational release in this span.

evidence.excerpt: We are also infusing AI into our creative apps as a co-pilot to help our customers and users work faster and smarter, with new models for images and vector graphics, and AI-powered video features natively integrated into our flagship products like Photoshop, Illustrator, and Premiere Pro.
evidence.review_reason: AI features are described as natively integrated into named creative applications; co-pilot is a product role, not a trial.

scenario.name: Bank operations AI capability build
assumptions: Fictional 200-person bank operations unit; not a client or a staffing estimate for JPMorgan/BAC.
Demand represents distinct, non-overlapping capability assignments. Candidate pools are disjoint across skills and routes.
Upfront training cost is $5,000 instruction plus 80 learning hours at $50 per hour; redeployment $5,000; recruiting and onboarding $24,000.

Annual recurring costs are incremental pay/license uplift ($12,000 training), backfill/opportunity cost ($42,000 redeployment), and fully loaded new-hire cost ($150,000). Existing base payroll is common to the decision and excluded.
Recurring costs apply to every candidate from month 1, including unsuccessful candidates. Benefits accrue only to expected successful capability after readiness. No salvage value, tax or inflation.
Success rates represent expected attainment, not guaranteed headcount. No attrition after attainment; no claim about displacement or headcount reduction.
Annual value is modeled gross incremental operating contribution per successful capability; it is neither estimated from filings nor a BLS wage.
